summary: Permit one earlier signed retry for a recently successful plain HTTP peer

replay.detail: Envelope receipt, duplicate handling, projection and replay are unchanged.

schema.detail: No durable table, index or data-format changes; retry credit is private task-local state.

rules.detail: No claim or checkpoint rule changes.

compatibility.detail: A qualifying peer may receive one additional off-cadence signed exchange after a typed before-header plain HTTP transport failure and a successful HEAD. When ordinary backoff reaches the first-HEAD started+30s cap, the advance can submit at the first successful HEAD probe (nominally 3s), up to ten times sooner relative to that cap; shorter already-due waits do not advance. This is a rate-policy change and may reach a loaded peer sooner. Before-header timeout does not prove absence of remote effects; normal authenticated duplicate handling is preserved. Signed overload, member refusal and Fabric grants retain precedence; HTTPS and unclassified failures do not advance.

downtime.detail: No migration or additional service interruption beyond a normal binary swap.

manual.detail: No new configuration or manual action.

recovery.detail: The opportunity starts absent, expires within five monotonic minutes of complete signed success, and is spent before export. Each success can earn one new opportunity: five minutes is a credit lifetime, not an aggregate request quota. One opportunity is a full exchange that can include compact/full rounds, follow-up requests, overload polls and checkpoint manifest pagination, not a constant POST count. Failed advancement resumes the original capped absolute deadline and ordinary backoff count; a new signed cooldown may extend it. Restart discards credit. Authentication, generation, routes, removal or expiry refuse further advanced submission and terminal success. A local admission refusal does not mark the peer down or reset its HTTP client. This draft does not certify three- or ten-second recovery, performance improvement or quarantine removal.
